9
A student attempts to find the density ρ of aluminium by taking measurements of a rectangular
sheet.
mass m = 51.6 ± 0.1 g
length l = 100.0 ± 0.1 cm
width w = 10.0 ± 0.1 cm
thickness t = 0.20 ± 0.01 mm
m
He uses the equation ρ =
t
w
l to calculate the density.
What is the calculated value of density with its uncertainty?
A
0.26 ± 0.01 g cm–3
B
0.26 ± 0.02 g cm–3
C
2.6 ± 0.1 g cm–3
D
2.6 ± 0.2 g cm–3

hints: Notice thickness $t = 0.20 \pm 0.01 \text{ mm}$ is in $\text{mm}$ while length and width are in $\text{cm}$, so convert $t$ to $\text{cm}$ before finding volume $wlt$.
For $\rho = m/(wlt)$ with multiply and divide, add the four fractional uncertainties $\Delta m/m + \Delta l/l + \Delta w/w + \Delta t/t$.

Compare the four percentages: thickness is $0.01/0.20 = 5\%$, much larger than mass, length and width, then multiply the total percentage by the $2.6 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ density to get the absolute uncertainty.
walkthrough: Convert thickness to consistent units: $t = 0.20 \text{ mm} = 0.020 \text{ cm}$. Then volume $V = wlt = 10.0 \times 100.0 \times 0.020 = 20 \text{ cm}^{3}$.
Calculate density: $\rho = m/V = 51.6/20 = 2.58 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, which rounds to $2.6 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ for the option format.
Calculate each fractional uncertainty: $\Delta m/m = 0.1/51.6 \approx 0.0019$, $\Delta l/l = 0.1/100.0 = 0.001$, $\Delta w/w = 0.1/10.0 = 0.01$, $\Delta t/t = 0.01/0.20 = 0.05$.
Add them for the product $wlt$ in the denominator: $\Delta \rho/\rho \approx 0.0019 + 0.001 + 0.01 + 0.05 \approx 0.063$ or $6.3\%$.
Convert to absolute uncertainty: $\Delta \rho \approx 0.063 \times 2.58 \approx 0.16 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, rounded to one significant figure as $\pm 0.2 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.
So the result is $2.6 \pm 0.2 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Value is a factor of 10 too small because thickness $0.20 \text{ mm}$ was not converted to $0.020 \text{ cm}$ before using $\text{g cm}^{-3}$.

B.explanation: Value is a factor of 10 too small from the $\text{mm}$ to $\text{cm}$ conversion, and the uncertainty does not match the correct density.

C.explanation: Density $2.6 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ is correct but $\pm 0.1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ is too small because the $5\%$ thickness uncertainty alone gives about $\pm 0.13 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: Density is about $2.6 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ and total fractional uncertainty of about $6.3\%$ gives absolute uncertainty of about $0.16 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, rounded to $\pm 0.2 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.
